title: Provincial Mobility Disadvantaged Transportation grants received every year (2016-2026)
summary: Every year council receives, as information, letters and payments from the Province of Manitoba's Mobility Disadvantaged Transportation Program (MDTP), which cost-shares the city's handi-transit / ACCESSible Transit service. Since the service was handed to the Pat Porter Active Living Centre in 2022, the city forwards the money to the centre.
status_detail: Routine: received as information at roughly two meetings a year, never debated. In April 2026 staff confirmed the province pays about $30,000 a year in two instalments, passed through to Pat Porter.
notes: Pre-2018 amounts not available (no minutes). The 2016-05-03 item was taken as information with no discussion.

title: Annual Handi-Transit financial reports accepted (2017-2021)
summary: While the city ran Handi-Transit itself, council accepted an audited Handi-Transit financial report each year (required for provincial cost-sharing). The motions passed without discussion.
status_detail: Accepted unanimously each time: 2017-03-07 (moved by Councillor Earl Funk, per transcript); R18-103 (May 1, 2018); R19-114 (May 7, 2019); R21-162 (Jul 20, 2021). No report found for the 2019 year in the minutes searched. After 2022 the service is a grant to Serving Seniors Inc.
figures: Auditors: Chambers Fraser (2017, 2018 reports); Reid and Miller (2020 report). Amounts not stated in minutes.
mover: E. Funk (2017, 2018); B. Hiebert (2019); J. Hiebert (2021)
notes: 2017-03-07: the transcript names Councillor Funk as mover; the seconder is not audible. 2017 has no minutes.

title: City applies for a provincial grant to replace a Handi-Transit van; province says no
summary: Council asked the province's Small Communities Transportation Fund for 50% of the cost of a new Handi Van (up to $50,000), with the city funding the rest in 2019. In August 2018 the province told the city it would not receive funding for the van (or for the sidewalk program applied for the same night).
status_detail: Application approved unanimously (R18-039); the province declined it (correspondence received Aug 7, 2018). Whether the city bought the van on its own was not found in the minutes.
figures: Grant request: 50% of van cost, max $50,000 (minutes R18-039).
notes: Seconder "Councillor Penner" in the transcript; minutes say C. Penner.

title: Steinbach Taxi asks council to regulate taxis under the new Vehicles for Hire Act; council decides against a by-law
summary: After the province's Bill 30 (Vehicles for Hire Act) handed taxi regulation to municipalities on Feb 28, 2018, Steinbach Taxi's president (P.J.) and a consultant (S.M.) asked council for a by-law that would recognise its 15 provincially issued licences, watch for illegal ride-sharing, and partner with the company; they also offered to expand handi-transit services. Councillor Zwaagstra asked whether this was a request to limit competition; Councillor Fehr said the province gave too little time and more research was needed. Mayor Goertzen asked administration for a report.
status_detail: Mayor Goertzen referred the request to administration. Per SteinbachOnline (May 2018), council then adopted administration's recommendation not to create a vehicle-for-hire by-law, on a motion by Councillor Zwaagstra, unanimously, at a committee meeting that is not in the regular minutes or recordings; Zwaagstra said a by-law would only limit competition. No by-law has been made since. Ride services are licensed as ordinary businesses, e.g. 'Tuk Tuk Taxi - Ride Service' business licence approved Nov 18, 2025 (R25-226, S. Penner / B. Hiebert).
figures: Steinbach Taxi: 17 full-time employees, 15 licences, 2 handi vans on the road (delegation, transcript 0:34:55).
reasons: study-first: complex issue, province gave little time; "we need a lot more research" (John Fehr); partners-do-it: questioned regulating at all; asked whether licence limits would just restrict competition (Michael Zwaagstra); partners-do-it: less regulation is best for competition between ride services and taxis (Cari Penner (per news))
public: Steinbach Taxi (P.J., president; S.M., consultant): Steinbach has no public transport so taxis fill a needed service, including for seniors and the disabled; asked for licence recognition, a check on illegal Facebook ride groups, and offered to expand handi-transit services.
notes: Speaker labels in this delegation are partly merged (e.g. 0:55:46 and 0:57:38); only clearly addressed turns are used. No follow-up report found. May 2018 decision from SteinbachOnline (peers.json), not re-fetched; committee meetings are not recorded.

title: Province advises Steinbach to "begin planning for a transit system now" in its 2018 Official Community Plan
summary: At the July 17, 2018 public hearing on the new Official Community Plan (By-law 2099), the province's Community and Regional Planning office (regional manager S.W.) recommended that Steinbach start planning for transit and make future development transit-supportive, noting the OCP expected 25,000 people in 10 years. City Planner Lacey Gaudet replied that a transportation plan was wanted 'within the future' but not immediately.
status_detail: The 2018 OCP was adopted (third reading R18-242, Oct 16, 2018) without a found transit policy. The next OCP (By-law 2244, 2025) added a policy (4.2.2.13) on future consideration/studies of the feasibility of public transportation, and the city's first Active Transportation Plan was accepted May 6, 2025. No transit plan or study has been commissioned.
figures: OCP population projection 25,000 in 10 years (provincial presentation, transcript 0:45:45).
reasons: study-first: a transportation plan is wanted in the future, but not immediately (Lacey Gaudet (City Planner))
public: Advice came from the Province of Manitoba (Community and Regional Planning), not residents.
notes: S.W. is a provincial official, shown by initials as a non-council speaker. Gaudet is identified as City Planner from the 2024-2025 speaker maps.

title: Handi-Transit handed to Serving Seniors Inc. (Pat Porter Active Living Centre) under a grant agreement
summary: After a study session, administration negotiated the 'Steinbach Accessible Transportation Services Agreement': the city grants funding to Serving Seniors Inc., which runs the service (now ACCESSible Transit) from early 2022, keeping basic service levels with room to expand. Council's condition was no significant change in cost. Councillors Zwaagstra and Siemens and Mayor Funk praised it as a 'natural fit' and a true partnership.
status_detail: Approved unanimously (R21-253). Serving Seniors / Pat Porter has run the service since 2022; the city's grant was $102,921.49 in 2022 (2022 grant summary, R23-039) and $105,000 in the 2026 financial plan.
figures: 2022 grant 'Serving Seniors - Transit' $102,921.49 (minutes R23-039, Feb 21, 2023); 2026 Accessible Transit grant $105,000 (2026 Financial Plan presentation, steinbach.ca).
reasons: cost: proceed only without a significant change in the cost of the service (Council (per administration)); partners-do-it: better delivered by a seniors organization; city provides a grant (Michael Zwaagstra)
notes: Agreement terms (hours, eligibility) are in the council package, not reviewed here. The service is now branded ACCESSible Transit (city website).

title: Mayor says the city is doing "due diligence" on transit but "it is very expensive" (news)
summary: In June 2023 Mayor Funk told SteinbachOnline the city was doing its due diligence on public transit, adding: 'Every time we talk, there is one common theme, it is very expensive.' This was not at a recorded council meeting.
status_detail: No study, report or budget item on general transit followed at any recorded meeting.
reasons: cost: transit is very expensive (SteinbachOnline, Jun 2023) (Earl Funk)
notes: Source: https://steinbachonline.com/articles/mayor-of-steinbach-says-city-is-doing-its-due-diligence-on-public-transit- (quoted in the existing answers/transit report; not re-fetched).

title: South East Equity Coalition presents transit survey; council rejects a bus loop and asks for costs (unrecorded session)
summary: On Feb 13, 2024, outside a recorded regular meeting, the South East Equity Coalition presented survey results on transportation needs. Per SteinbachOnline, Councillor Zwaagstra said a fixed loop 'would be very expensive and you run the risk of having empty buses' and that the city should not compete with taxis; Councillor Susan Penner agreed a bus loop would not work and wanted 'the cost analysis, how this would be funded, what grants are available'; Councillor Damian Penner said exploring alternatives was 'something that we have an obligation to start looking at exploring'.
status_detail: No motion, study or budget item followed; the coalition went on to draft its own on-demand plan (May 2025).
figures: Coalition survey of 751 people (mostly its client groups): 32% walk, 23% get rides, 12% take taxis (per existing report / SteinbachOnline).
reasons: cost: very expensive; risk of empty buses (news) (Michael Zwaagstra); partners-do-it: don't set up a system that competes with taxis (news) (Michael Zwaagstra); study-first: wants cost analysis, funding and grants identified (news) (Susan Penner)
public: South East Equity Coalition (organization) presented survey results and later an on-demand plan.
notes: Source: https://www.steinbachonline.com/articles/steinbach-council-speaks-on-public-transit-we-have-an-obligation-to-start-looking-at-exploring- . Not a recorded meeting; quotes are from news, not video, and were not re-fetched.

title: At an infill-housing hearing, the applicant and a resident link density to future public transit
summary: At the Mar 19, 2024 public hearing on a Kingdom Home Building infill project near the hospital, the applicant's representative (L.W.) said infill supports the feasibility of public transit, 'which we hope to see one day soon'; a resident (H.W.) argued density increases access to public transportation and reduces traffic. Council did not discuss transit.
status_detail: Transit was raised only as a supporting argument; no council response on transit.
public: L.W. (Kingdom Home Building, applicant) and H.W. (resident) connected density with future transit.

title: New Official Community Plan adds a policy that the city "could consider" public transportation
summary: The 2025 Official Community Plan (By-law 2244) added policy 4.2.2.13 on future consideration/studies of the feasibility of public transportation; the province welcomed the 'mention of public transportation'. At the Apr 1, 2025 hearing a resident (A.B.) asked how seniors would get around without cars; Mayor Funk replied that active transportation was welcome but 'we are the automobile city'. Councillor Siemens listed 'just starting to understand what public transportation looks like' among the plan's themes.
status_detail: Adopted unanimously: recommendations accepted Dec 3, 2024 (R24-234), first and second reading Apr 1, 2025 (R25-069, R25-070), third reading Sep 16, 2025 (R25-184). The policy is permissive ('could consider'); no feasibility study has been commissioned.
figures: OCP policy 4.2.2.13 (Dec 3, 2024 and Apr 1, 2025 council packages).
reasons: car-city: "we are the automobile city" and vehicles must keep a place on the road (Earl Funk); study-first: policy commits only to future consideration/studies (Council (OCP))
public: A.B. (resident) asked how seniors would get around if they cannot use their cars and objected to the by-law.
mover: S. Penner (R24-234); J. Siemens (1st); J. Hiebert (2nd); S. Penner (3rd)
seconder: D. Penner (R24-234); M. Zwaagstra (1st); B. Hiebert (2nd); M. Zwaagstra (3rd)
notes: The consultant is shown by firm (WSP), as in the existing report.

title: Mayor reports Cities Caucus push to restore 50/50 provincial transit operating funding
summary: Reporting from the Association of Manitoba Municipalities convention, Mayor Funk said public transit is 'very dear to a couple of the bigger cities' (Brandon, Winnipeg) and that the urban centres would advocate a return to 50/50 provincial operating funding because 'the cost is killing the communities that are providing transit'.
status_detail: Advocacy item; no council motion. Steinbach itself runs no general transit that would benefit.
reasons: cost: transit costs are "killing" the communities that provide it (Earl Funk); provincial-responsibility: province should restore its 50% share of operating costs (Earl Funk)
notes: The turn starts at 0:00:00; the transit remark is about 3:49 into the video.

title: First Active Transportation Plan accepted; councillors split on moving people beyond cars
summary: Council accepted the city's first consultant-prepared Active Transportation Plan (walking, cycling, pathways; about $11 million in total over the long term). Councillor Siemens said the city's planning had always been about moving vehicles, not people; Councillor Zwaagstra said active transportation must not hinder vehicle traffic. In a later parking debate (Nov 18, 2025) Zwaagstra said most Steinbach residents, even on Main Street, have cars. The plan does not cover public transit.
status_detail: Accepted unanimously (R25-096) as a guide; not a transit plan.
reasons: car-city: people drive, especially in winter; planning must not impede vehicles (Michael Zwaagstra); cost: price tags are very high; much is far in the future (Michael Zwaagstra)
notes: The Nov 18, 2025 quote comes from a parking variance debate, used here for the car-dependence reasoning.

title: Coalition's "LinK Transit" on-demand van plan gets verbal support only (news)
summary: On May 13, 2025 (not a recorded regular meeting) the South East Equity Coalition presented 'LinK Transit', an on-demand service with four vans run by the Pat Porter Active Living Centre, asking for $6,000 in seed money, an endorsement and help with grants. Per SteinbachOnline the city gave verbal support only; a later budget request for vans was not advanced, and in July 2026 council told CBC it needs 'a viable plan' before acting. The mayor and council were invited to ride Winkler's on-demand van and did not attend.
status_detail: No motion, endorsement, seed funding or grant application found at any recorded meeting through Nov 3, 2026.
figures: Plan: ~$957,000 start-up, ~$96,000/yr operating, 4 vans; ask $6,000 seed money (news, per existing report).
reasons: study-first: needs a viable plan first (Council (to CBC, Jul 2026)); wait-for-funding: no funding committed; grants to be identified (news) (Council)
public: South East Equity Coalition (organization) proposed the plan and continues to press for transit.
notes: Sources (from existing report, not re-fetched): https://content.goldenwestapps.com/node/174085 ; https://content.goldenwestapps.com/node/178095 ; https://steinbachonline.com/articles/public-transit-remains-high-priority-for-southeast-equity-coalition ; https://ca.news.yahoo.com/steinbach-coalition-looks-winklers-wisdom-171708389.html . No transcript mentions the coalition.

title: Public transportation listed as an eligible use of a $200,000 provincial safety grant; staff recommend cameras and a CSO truck
summary: Presenting an unexpected $200,000 provincial public safety grant, staff listed 'public transportation' among Community Safety and Well-Being plan priorities council could support, but recommended $65,000 for a second CSO truck and $135,000 for security cameras. Council deferred the item for more discussion.
status_detail: Deferred to a later committee/special meeting (Aug 11 discussed); no transit allocation proposed; final decision not found in minutes searched.

title: KodaGo, a Steinbach-built ride-share app, asks the city to partner; mayor invites a letter
summary: KodaGo's founder (J.O.) described starting the app because there was no bus or return Uber to Steinbach; with 246 users it serves southeast Manitoba and asked for a city partnership focused on medical appointments and airport trips. A Councillor Penner praised private innovation as 'often far superior to public spent dollars' while leaving public transit open for the future; Mayor Funk said a partnership would go beyond a letter of support, that the city partners only with its accessible transit service, and asked for a letter.
status_detail: No letter, motion or partnership appears in transcripts or minutes through Nov 3, 2026.
reasons: partners-do-it: private innovation fills gaps better than public spending (Damian Penner (medium confidence)); partners-do-it: private enterprise sees a need and builds a product (Earl Funk)
public: J.O. (KodaGo founder) asked for a partnership for medical and airport trips; no bus or return Uber to Steinbach.
notes: Minutes spell the founder "Justus Oladele"; shown by initials. The Penner remarks are medium confidence (speaker map vs minutes conflict).
